slides.reasoning: Design A balances a huge lime ARR figure, a clean labeled metric stack, and a full-width rising chart with axis labels, whereas Design B leaves a large empty upper-right void, crowds its metric rows against the chart's left edge, and lets the footer chart caption float awkwardly beneath the axis.

Design A delivers the illustrated journey the brief asks for with clay dominance, hand-drawn marks and a taped note, while Design B reverts to three text columns under the route, uses a soft gradient blush field that dilutes the clay palette, and shows uneven label placement around the path.

Design A's tangled-lines vs. clean-graph contrast plus the dominant $780k ROI block reads instantly and fills the frame, while Design B's before/after boxes are text-heavy, its ROI band sits low with an awkward CTA overlap into the caption zone, and bottom whitespace feels unresolved.

Design B's allocation ring is legible with clearly separated segments and a tidy portfolio-construction table, whereas Design A's dim double-ring reads muddy at thumbnail size and its '20%' label collides with the tick marks/ring edge.

Design A's exploded driver stack with leader-line callouts is genuinely cinematic and keeps the product the hero, while Design B's flat headphone render, striped background, and spec table feel brochure-like with cramped labels near the ear-cup edge.

Design A presents one coherent chart system with variance markers, a scorecard column, and an emphatically flagged activation gap in balanced whitespace; Design B is competent but leaves a large empty block under its regional bars and stacks the activation bar tightly against chart captions.

Design B's four parallel transit lines, interchange bar, pillar sidebar, and dark north-star footer form a tighter civic-wayfinding system, while Design A's converging lines crowd labels between routes and its right side mixes measures with an explanatory paragraph unevenly.

Design A's chevron roadmap with a real week ruler, diamond gates, and owner lines is more dynamic and information-dense without collision, while Design B relies on flat phase blocks plus gate boxes and leaves a wide empty gap between the gate row and the footer band.

Design A pairs a bold 4C loop with an annotated worked example whose marker-style callouts map to each step, delivering the facilitation feel; Design B's loop has label lines drifting oddly, the '4C / repeat until agreed' mark sits half-hidden behind the ring, and the right column is sparse.

Design A supplies the memorable 68% waffle plus a genuinely diagrammed three-app journey with confidence-break annotations, while Design B's dot array is disconnected from its numeral, the app chain is thin and floating, and the footer band lets sample text wrap raggedly to a lone word.

Design A creates a true auditorium moment with the outlined dissolving headline, silhouetted crowd, and visible/hidden UI sketches, whereas Design B's stacked title overlaps 'THE' into 'DISAPPEARING' clumsily and its boxed lists read as a generic slide rather than a keynote.

Design A's split orange/powder-blue composition with oversized editorial numerals gives strong hierarchy and integrates customer voice and priorities elegantly, while Design B's four-metric row with badge chips and two boxed panels is flatter and more conventional.

Design A makes the corridor map the full-bleed emotional centerpiece with a field-ledger overlay, legend, and scale bar; Design B's map is cleaner but generic, and its left panel crams the ask into a narrow column with the CTA button pinned tightly to the lower edge.

Design A's enormous 'a' with yellow counter, red callouts, and baseline/x-height rules is far more instructional and Bauhaus-precise, while Design B's letterform is smaller, its baseline rule cuts through the glyph awkwardly, and the counter label points into empty space below the letter.

Design A's giant citrus macro, stacked audience bar, and dotted-leader partnership list form a confident editorial composition, whereas Design B's flat vector 'pizza' graphic reads as clipart, its metric row nearly touches the partnership list, and 'above' wraps into the divider.
